project.name: ai-trip
project.description: AI-powered full-stack travel itinerary planner built on Nuxt 4 that combines Gemini-generated, JSON-structured itineraries with Google Maps-verified locations, and includes collaboration, expenses, travel documents, and 3D globe visualizations. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: layover-tips.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that generates AI layover recommendations for a given airport, duration, and visa status using Gemini with Google Search grounding; results are cached for 30 days and gated by auth and AI credit consumption.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Nuxt defineCachedFunction with a custom cache key plus Vercel AI SDK Output.object for typed structured generation.

nodes.name: generateLayoverTips
nodes.summary: Cached Gemini call that produces structured layover tips (recommendation, suggestions, transit info, return-by time), enabling Google Search tool use and respecting visa restrictions.

nodes.name: usage.get.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny GET endpoint that returns the current authenticated user's remaining AI credit usage.

nodes.name: [...all].ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt catch-all route that forwards every /api/auth/* request to the BetterAuth handler exported from server/lib/auth.

nodes.name: check-passport-expiry.get.ts
nodes.summary: Cron-invoked GET endpoint that delegates passport expiry notification scanning to a server task, intended to be triggered on a daily schedule.

nodes.name: import-visa-data.get.ts
nodes.summary: Cron-invoked GET endpoint that triggers the visa-data import server task to refresh visa requirement data from upstream sources.

nodes.name: exchange-rate.get.ts
nodes.summary: Authenticated GET endpoint that returns the exchange rate between two ISO currency codes, proxying to the Frankfurter API with a 6-hour server cache.

nodes.name: [id].delete.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE endpoint that removes a single flight owned by the authenticated user after UUID validation.

nodes.name: [id].get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that returns a flight by id and opportunistically refreshes airline/status data from the flight API when the cached record is stale.

nodes.name: shouldRefresh
nodes.summary: Decides whether to refetch flight data: always refresh on first load, never refresh more than 24h after arrival, otherwise refresh when the last fetch is older than two hours.

nodes.name: [id].patch.ts
nodes.summary: PATCH endpoint that updates user-editable flight fields (e.g., notes, manual overrides) for the authenticated owner of a flight.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that lists all flights belonging to the authenticated user, with optional trip relations loaded.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that creates a flight record, enriching it with airline/airport/time data fetched from the flight lookup API.

nodes.name: [token].post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that accepts a trip invite by hashing the incoming token, validating expiry and email match, then activating the trip member record.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses node:crypto createHash to compare against stored SHA-256 invite hashes rather than raw tokens.

nodes.name: [templateId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE endpoint that removes a user-owned packing template after UUID validation.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that lists all packing templates saved by the authenticated user.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that persists a new packing template (name + item list) for the authenticated user after schema validation.

nodes.name: details.get.ts
nodes.summary: Authenticated GET endpoint that returns enriched Google Places details (name, address, rating, photos) for a given place id.

nodes.name: photo.get.ts
nodes.summary: Authenticated photo proxy endpoint that fetches and returns a Google Places photo binary, enforcing that the photo reference belongs to the given placeId and adding long-lived cache headers.

nodes.name: search.get.ts
nodes.summary: Authenticated GET endpoint that performs a Google Places text search and returns candidate matches for AI itinerary resolution.

nodes.name: [token].get.ts
nodes.summary: Public GET endpoint that resolves a trip by its share token and returns only public-safe itinerary fields, lazily enriching activity photos from Google Places when missing.
nodes.languageNotes: Strips private fields (preferences, costs, notes) and uses Promise.allSettled to enrich photos without failing the whole response.

nodes.name: photo.get.ts
nodes.summary: Public photo proxy for shared trips that returns a Google Places photo binary scoped to the trip identified by the share token, without requiring authentication.

nodes.name: stats.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that aggregates per-user travel statistics (total trips, completed trips, total days, countries visited, activities, distance traveled, flights) across owned and shared trips.
nodes.languageNotes: Parallelizes independent Drizzle queries with Promise.all and uses raw sql template literals for OR conditions across owned/shared trips.

nodes.name: [id].delete.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE endpoint that removes a trip owned by the authenticated user after UUID validation and access checks.

nodes.name: [id].get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that returns a single trip with its days, activities, and travel segments hydrated via getTripWithRelations.

nodes.name: [id].put.ts
nodes.summary: PUT endpoint that updates trip metadata and, when dates change, reconciles itinerary days by inserting missing dates, deleting out-of-range ones, and renumbering kept days atomically.
nodes.languageNotes: Branches on import.meta.dev to use db.transaction (node-postgres) vs db.batch (neon-http) because the two Drizzle drivers expose different atomicity primitives.

nodes.name: range.put.ts
nodes.summary: PUT endpoint that applies an accommodation (lodging) to a contiguous date range on a trip, propagating address/lat/lng to each affected itinerary day.

nodes.name: [activityId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt DELETE route handler that removes an activity from a trip after verifying the caller has editor or owner access.

nodes.name: [activityId].put.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt PUT route handler that updates an activity's fields (name, time, notes, cost, etc.) with validated body data and trip access checks.

nodes.name: comments.get.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt GET route handler that lists all comments attached to a specific activity, ordered by creation time.

nodes.name: comments.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that creates a new comment on an activity for collaborative trip discussions.

nodes.name: enrich.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that re-enriches a single activity with Google Places metadata (rating, photos, opening hours, coordinates).

nodes.name: participants.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that adds a trip member as a participant of a specific activity for collaborative planning.

nodes.name: [userId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt DELETE route handler that removes a participant from an activity, enforcing trip access permissions.

nodes.name: vote.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that casts or toggles a user's vote (up/down/none) on a proposed activity for group decision-making.

nodes.name: votes.get.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt GET route handler that returns all votes for an activity so the UI can render tallies and per-user vote state.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that creates a new activity on a trip day, pulling cost estimates from Google place price data and recomputing travel segments.

nodes.name: [checklistId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt DELETE route handler that removes a checklist and its items from a trip after permission checks.

nodes.name: [checklistId].put.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt PUT route handler that updates a checklist's metadata such as title or description.

nodes.name: [itemId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt DELETE route handler that removes a single item from a trip checklist.

nodes.name: [itemId].put.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt PUT route handler that updates a checklist item's label, completion state, or notes.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that appends a new item to an existing checklist within a trip.

nodes.name: load-template.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that hydrates a checklist from a saved template, inserting all template items into the current checklist.

nodes.name: save-as-template.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that snapshots an existing checklist's items as a reusable template owned by the current user.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt GET route handler that lists all checklists for a trip including their items, for the trip planning UI.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that creates a new empty checklist on a trip.

nodes.name: convert-currency.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that converts all monetary fields on a trip (activities, accommodations, budget) from one currency to another using exchange rates.

nodes.name: date-change-preview.get.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt GET route handler that previews the effects of changing trip start/end dates, reporting which days would be added or removed.

nodes.name: accommodation.put.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt PUT route handler that updates the accommodation (hotel/lodging) details for a specific itinerary day.

nodes.name: ai.post.ts
nodes.summary: Core Nuxt POST route that dispatches Gemini-powered day-level edits (add, remove, modify, optimize, reschedule, fill gaps, accommodation) with prompt sanitization, AI credit gating, Google Maps enrichment, and segment recomputation.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest handler in the codebase — orchestrates the full AI-to-itinerary pipeline including credit consumption, prompt validation, intent routing, place enrichment, and transport segment computation.

nodes.name: enrich.post.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt POST route handler that re-runs Google Places enrichment for all activities on a single day and recomputes travel segments between them.

nodes.name: notes.put.ts
nodes.summary: Nuxt PUT route handler that updates the free-text notes attached to a specific itinerary day.

nodes.name: reorder.put.ts
nodes.summary: Nitro server route that reorders activities within a day and reassigns to a different day, recomputing travel segments via Google Maps after the move.

nodes.name: restore.post.ts
nodes.summary: Restores a previously soft-deleted day or its activities and rebuilds the transport segments for the affected day.

nodes.name: segments.get.ts
nodes.summary: Returns the list of transport segments computed between activities for a specific trip day.

nodes.name: segments.post.ts
nodes.summary: Triggers (re)computation of transport segments between activities for a given trip day using Google Distance Matrix.

nodes.name: discuss.post.ts
nodes.summary: Handles the AI discussion endpoint: validates the chat thread, builds rich trip context, invokes the Gemini discuss agent with tool calls, and returns assistant replies plus draft itinerary proposals.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Vercel AI SDK tool-calling pattern with a typed Proposal contract and sanitizes user prompt input before LLM invocation.

nodes.name: buildTripContext
nodes.summary: Loads the trip with all relations and serializes destination, dates, preferences, the focused day's activities, and nearby days into a compact context string for the LLM system prompt.

nodes.name: describeToolCall
nodes.summary: Produces a short human-readable description of a tool call entry (id plus truncated query/args) for logging or display in the chat trace.

nodes.name: [documentId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: Deletes a single uploaded document from a trip after verifying the caller owns or belongs to the trip.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: Lists all documents attached to a trip for the authorized caller.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: Accepts a multipart upload, validates file size/type, stores the document blob, and creates a documents row linked to the trip.

nodes.name: [expenseId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: Deletes a single expense row from a trip after permission checks.

nodes.name: [expenseId].put.ts
nodes.summary: Updates an existing trip expense (amount, category, description, payer) after validating input with Zod.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: Returns all expenses recorded against a trip for the authorized member.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: Creates a new expense entry on a trip with amount, currency, category and optional split-among-members association.

nodes.name: flights.get.ts
nodes.summary: Returns flight records for a trip, lazily re-fetching from AeroDataBox when the row uses an outdated lookup schema version, with a 24h cooldown guard against retry storms.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a forward-only schema-version migration pattern: increments lookupSchemaVersion on success and stamps apiLastFetchedAt on failure to enforce a cooldown.

nodes.name: maybeMigrateRow
nodes.summary: Re-fetches a flight row from AeroDataBox if its stored lookupSchemaVersion is older than the current one, honoring a 24h cooldown to prevent looping on failures.

nodes.name: [ideaId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: Removes a single idea from a trip's idea board after authorization checks.

nodes.name: promote.post.ts
nodes.summary: Promotes an idea-board entry into a real itinerary activity: enriches cost from the Google Place data, inserts the activity, and rebuilds the day's transport segments.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: Lists all idea-board entries for a trip for the authorized caller.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: Creates a new idea entry attached to a trip's idea board with title, notes and an optional resolved Google place reference.

nodes.name: logs.get.ts
nodes.summary: Returns the chronological activity log entries for a trip (edits, AI actions, member changes) for display in the activity feed.

nodes.name: [memberId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: Removes a member from a trip; only the trip owner may invoke this and the owner cannot remove themselves.

nodes.name: [memberId].put.ts
nodes.summary: Updates a member's role on a trip (owner/editor/viewer), enforcing owner-only mutation rights.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: Lists all members of a trip joined with user profile data (display name, avatar) for the membership UI.

nodes.name: invite.post.ts
nodes.summary: Invites a user to a trip by email: creates an invitation token, persists the pending member record, and dispatches an invite email via the mail provider.

nodes.name: leave.post.ts
nodes.summary: Lets the current authenticated user voluntarily leave a trip; refuses the request if the caller is the sole owner.

nodes.name: participants.get.ts
nodes.summary: Returns the flattened participants list for a trip (members plus invited but unregistered guests) used by the expense splitter and activity assignment UI.

nodes.name: apply.post.ts
nodes.summary: Applies an AI-generated itinerary proposal to a trip: persists the suggested activities, normalizes transport modes and recomputes the day's segments.

nodes.name: refresh-cost-estimates.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that refreshes activity cost estimates by fanning out Google Places lookups for activities missing a costEstimate and updating them in parallel.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Promise.allSettled to tolerate partial failures across Google Maps calls; relies on cached getPlaceDetails for performance.

nodes.name: [reservationId].delete.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE endpoint that removes a reservation from a trip after verifying owner/editor access.

nodes.name: [reservationId].put.ts
nodes.summary: PUT endpoint that updates a reservation's fields after validating ownership and trip access.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that lists all reservations attached to a trip for any authorized member.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that creates a new reservation on a trip and logs the action to the trip audit trail.

nodes.name: review.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that runs an AI-powered itinerary review for either a single day or the whole trip, returning structured feedback.

nodes.name: share.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that toggles a trip's public share token (generates a new UUID with 30-day expiry, or revokes the existing one).

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that lists the user's own trips plus actively-shared trips with role tagging (owner/editor/viewer), paginated.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that creates a new trip, enforces a 50-trip per-user limit, and auto-generates itinerary day rows for the date range.

nodes.name: [id].delete.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE endpoint that removes a user passport after verifying ownership.

nodes.name: [id].patch.ts
nodes.summary: PATCH endpoint that partially updates a user passport, ensuring isDefault is exclusive across the user's passports.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that returns all passports configured for the authenticated user.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that adds a new passport to the user profile, enforcing default-passport exclusivity.

nodes.name: profile.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that returns the authenticated user's profile data.

nodes.name: profile.put.ts
nodes.summary: PUT endpoint that updates the authenticated user's profile fields.

nodes.name: check-all.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint returning visa status for every destination country for a given passport, used to render visa heat maps.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a priority map to pick the most favorable visa status when multiple records exist for the same destination.

nodes.name: check.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that resolves visa requirements for a single destination across one or all of the user's passports, returning the most favorable result.
nodes.languageNotes: Short-circuits to visa-free when destination matches any of the user's passports; otherwise queries visaRequirements and sorts by priority.

nodes.name: details.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that returns enriched visa requirements (requirements, processing time, cost, notes) for a specific passport-destination pair.

nodes.name: [countryCode].delete.ts
nodes.summary: DELETE endpoint that removes a country from the user's visited-countries list.

nodes.name: index.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that lists all countries the authenticated user has marked as visited, in layover, or want-to-visit.

nodes.name: index.post.ts
nodes.summary: POST endpoint that upserts a visited country entry (visited/layover/want_to_visit) keyed by user and country code.

nodes.name: weather.get.ts
nodes.summary: GET endpoint that fetches a daily weather forecast from Open-Meteo for trip dates, falling back to last year's historical data when dates exceed the 16-day forecast window.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Nitro's defineCachedFunction (6h TTL) with a custom key based on rounded lat/lng plus date range; transparently switches between forecast and historical APIs.

nodes.name: shiftDateByYear
nodes.summary: Helper that shifts an ISO date string by a given number of years, used to map between current trip dates and the corresponding historical dates from last year.

nodes.name: custom-types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines a Drizzle ORM custom column type that transparently encrypts/decrypts text values at the driver layer using the project's encryption helpers and ENCRYPTION_KEY env var.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Drizzle's customType helper with fromDriver/toDriver hooks to wrap PG text columns with symmetric encryption.

nodes.name: encryptedText
nodes.summary: Factory creating a Drizzle text column that encrypts on write and decrypts on read, throwing if ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Database client entry point that exports the Drizzle ORM instance bound to the project schema for use across server routes.

nodes.name: activities
nodes.summary: Core itinerary activity table storing Google-Maps-enriched location data (place_id, lat/lng, rating, photos, opening hours) per itinerary day with cost and timing metadata.

nodes.name: account
nodes.summary: BetterAuth account table storing OAuth provider credentials and tokens per user.

nodes.name: session
nodes.summary: BetterAuth session table tracking active user sessions with expiry, IP, and user agent.

nodes.name: user
nodes.summary: BetterAuth user table storing core account profile fields (name, email, verification status, image).

nodes.name: verification
nodes.summary: BetterAuth verification table holding short-lived tokens for email and credential verification flows.

nodes.name: checklist_items
nodes.summary: Individual checklist line items belonging to a trip checklist with completion state and sort order.

nodes.name: checklists
nodes.summary: Trip-scoped checklist container grouping packing/preparation items.

nodes.name: expenses
nodes.summary: Trip expense records optionally linked to a specific activity, with amount, category, and paid-at timestamp.

nodes.name: trips
nodes.summary: Top-level trip record owned by a user with destination, dates, status, preferences JSON, budget, and currency.

nodes.name: itinerary_days
nodes.summary: Per-day breakdown of a trip including the day's accommodation place_id, address, and coordinates.

nodes.name: travel_segments
nodes.summary: Computed travel legs between consecutive activities storing duration/distance and transport mode from the Distance Matrix API.

nodes.name: trip_ideas
nodes.summary: Candidate places saved against a trip but not yet scheduled into the itinerary, enriched with Google Places data.

nodes.name: activity_log
nodes.summary: Audit log capturing user actions on a trip (action, description, metadata JSON) for collaboration history.

nodes.name: ai_usage
nodes.summary: Per-user monthly counter of AI prompt invocations for quota tracking and rate limiting.

nodes.name: trip_members
nodes.summary: Trip membership and pending invite records with role, invited_by, invite_token, and expiry for collaborative trips.

nodes.name: activity_comments
nodes.summary: Free-text comments attached to an activity by trip members for discussion.

nodes.name: activity_votes
nodes.summary: Up/down votes from trip members against activities to converge on group preferences.

nodes.name: reservations
nodes.summary: Bookings made for a trip (flight, hotel, etc.) with status, confirmation number, provider, amount, and date range.

nodes.name: packing_templates
nodes.summary: Reusable packing-list templates either user-owned or global, holding items as JSON for quick checklist seeding.

nodes.name: documents
nodes.summary: Trip- or reservation-scoped document references (URL, size, MIME) uploaded by a user — e.g. tickets, hotel confirmations.

nodes.name: activity_participants
nodes.summary: Join table marking which trip members will participate in a given activity.

nodes.name: visited_countries
nodes.summary: Per-user record of countries visited with ISO code, visit date, and optional notes for travel history.

nodes.name: user_profiles
nodes.summary: Extended user profile data including nationality used for visa requirement lookups.

nodes.name: visa_cache
nodes.summary: Cached visa-requirement records keyed by passport+destination with status, stay limits, cost, and source attribution.

nodes.name: user_passports
nodes.summary: Multi-passport support per user with country code, optional label, and a default flag for visa flows.

nodes.name: flights
nodes.summary: Flight tracking records with flight number, airports, times, terminal/gate, status, and the raw external API response cached for refresh.

nodes.name: visa_requirements
nodes.summary: Replacement visa requirement lookup table keyed by passport+destination superseding visa_cache.

nodes.name: re-encrypt-data.ts
nodes.summary: One-off Postgres maintenance script that decrypts sensitive columns with an old SHA-256 derived key and re-encrypts them with a new HKDF-derived key inside a transaction.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Node's crypto primitives (createCipheriv/createDecipheriv with aes-256-gcm) and runs the work inside a single pg client transaction with rollback on failure.

nodes.name: deriveKeyOld
nodes.summary: Derives the legacy 32-byte encryption key from a secret by SHA-256 hashing it directly, matching the previous key-derivation scheme used in production.

nodes.name: deriveKeyNew
nodes.summary: Derives the new 32-byte encryption key using HKDF over the secret with a fixed salt and info string, aligning with the upgraded key-derivation scheme.

nodes.name: decryptWithKey
nodes.summary: Decodes a base64 ciphertext payload, splits it into IV/authTag/encrypted segments, and decrypts with aes-256-gcm using the supplied key.

nodes.name: encryptWithKey
nodes.summary: Generates a random 12-byte IV and encrypts a plaintext value with aes-256-gcm, returning a base64 string concatenating IV, auth tag, and ciphertext.

nodes.name: reEncryptTable
nodes.summary: For a given table/column pair, iterates every row, decrypts the value with the old key, re-encrypts it with the new key, and writes it back via a parameterized UPDATE.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entrypoint that connects to Postgres, begins a transaction, calls reEncryptTable for each encrypted column set, then commits or rolls back on error before releasing the pool.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what AI Trip actually does: a full-stack travel planner that combines structured AI itinerary generation with Google Maps-verified place data. The README lays out the core philosophy that drives every architectural choice ahead — JSON-driven itineraries instead of chat responses, no hallucinated locations, and a map-first UX. Skim the feature list and the AI + Maps pipeline diagram before diving in; the rest of the tour will follow that pipeline end-to-end.

tour.title: Nuxt Configuration & App Shell
tour.description: Nuxt is the runtime that wires the frontend (Vue 3) and the backend (Nitro) into a single project. `nuxt.config.ts` declares all the modules (UI, fonts, image, PWA, color-mode), exposes runtime config for secrets (Gemini key, Google Maps key, BetterAuth secret), and configures the Nitro deployment target. `app/app.vue` is the Vue root that mounts the layout system, the page outlet, and the PWA update prompt — every screen you'll see later is rendered through this component.
tour.languageLesson: Nuxt 4 separates the client app under `app/` from the server under `server/`, but both share a single `nuxt.config.ts`. Auto-imports mean components, composables, and server utils don't need explicit imports — Nuxt scans conventional folders at build time.

tour.title: Presentation Layer: Pages & Layouts
tour.description: Building on the app shell from Step 2, the presentation layer organizes screens via Nuxt's file-based routing. `app/pages/index.vue` is the marketing landing page, while `app/pages/trips/[id].vue` is the main workspace where users edit an itinerary, view the map, and trigger AI updates — this page is the visual hub the rest of the codebase serves. Layouts in `app/layouts/` wrap pages with shell chrome: `app.vue` provides the authenticated sidebar/topbar, and the auth middleware guards every protected route.

tour.title: The AI Dock & Map UI
tour.description: Two components carry the bulk of user interaction. `AiDock.vue` is the floating chat-like surface where users type intents ("add a sushi place near the hotel", "optimize day 2") — it does NOT render free-form chat; it collects intent and triggers the structured proposal pipeline you'll see in Step 7. `TripMap.vue` renders the Google Maps view with markers for every activity on a given day, color-coded by type, and is the map-first half of the philosophy from the README.

tour.title: Client Composables: AI, Maps, Places
tour.description: Composables are Vue's answer to React hooks — reusable reactive logic. The AI dock and trip page lean on three key ones. `useGoogleMaps.ts` lazy-loads the Maps JS SDK only when needed (keeps initial bundle small). `usePlaceSearch.ts` debounces autocomplete queries through the backend so the Google Places API key never ships to the browser. `useGenerateFullItinerary.ts` orchestrates the "generate the whole trip from scratch" flow with a confirmation modal before spending AI credits.
tour.languageLesson: Vue composables are plain functions starting with `use` that return reactive `ref`/`computed` values. Unlike React hooks, they have no "rules of hooks" — they can be called conditionally — because reactivity is tracked via Proxies, not call order.

tour.title: The AI Orchestration Endpoint
tour.description: This Nitro route is the heart of the application — the README calls it out by name. When a user submits an AI intent from the dock, it lands here. The handler authenticates the request, deducts AI credits, sanitizes input, then hands off to `processUserRequest` in the domain layer (Step 7). The 10 direct imports — db client, schema, AI engine, enrichment, segments, sanitize, schemas, ai-limits, transport — are exactly the abstractions a single AI request needs to touch, making this file a perfect cross-section of the whole architecture.
tour.languageLesson: Nitro file-based routes use the suffix convention: `ai.post.ts` only handles POST, `[id]` becomes a dynamic param, and brackets work for both files and folders. Default export from `defineEventHandler` is the handler.

tour.title: Domain Layer: AI Engine, Proposals, Enrichment
tour.description: The domain layer in `server/lib/` is where the AI + Maps pipeline really lives. `ai.ts` exposes `processUserRequest`, which dispatches to `handleAdd`/`handleRemove`/`handleOptimize`/`handleReschedule`/`handleFillGaps`/`handleAccommodation` based on detected intent — each producing a structured proposal, never a free-form reply. `proposals.ts` defines the discriminated-union proposal schema and applies accepted proposals to the database. `ai-tools.ts` registers Mastra/AI SDK tools (search_place, distance_matrix) so Gemini can call Google Maps itself during generation.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript discriminated unions (e.g. `type Proposal = { kind: 'add', ... } | { kind: 'remove', ... }`) let the compiler narrow on the `kind` field — every branch of the proposal-apply switch is type-safe without manual casting.

tour.title: Google Maps Facade & Place Enrichment
tour.description: The README's strongest rule is "AI must NEVER invent places" — these two files enforce it. `google-maps.ts` is the single cached facade over Google Maps Platform (Places Text Search, Place Details, Distance Matrix) — every other server file goes through it, which is why it has one of the highest fan-in counts in the codebase. `enrich.ts` takes raw AI-suggested place names and resolves each one to a real Google Place, attaching coords, ratings, photos, and opening hours before anything is persisted. If Google can't find it, the proposal is rejected.

tour.title: Drizzle Schema Barrel & Core Tables
tour.description: Once a proposal is approved and enriched, it persists through Drizzle ORM. `server/db/schema/index.ts` is a barrel re-exporting every table — 95 other files import from it, making it the single largest fan-in node in the codebase. The schema files model the domain: `trips.ts` is the top-level trip with destination/dates/budget/preferences JSON, `itineraries.ts` breaks each trip into days with accommodation pins, and `activities.ts` holds the enriched Google Places (place_id, lat/lng, rating, photos, opening hours) — mirroring the `EnrichedLocation` interface from CLAUDE.md.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle defines tables as TypeScript constants (e.g. `pgTable('trips', { ... })`) and infers row types from them. Unlike Prisma, there's no codegen step — your IDE gets full table/column autocomplete straight from the schema files.

tour.title: Database Client & Migrations
tour.description: `server/db/index.ts` exports the Drizzle client bound to the schema from Step 9 — also one of the highest fan-in nodes since virtually every API route imports it. `drizzle.config.ts` points drizzle-kit at the Postgres dialect, the schema folder, and the migrations output. The initial migration `0000_greedy_kronos.sql` is the baseline that creates the entire core schema in one shot: auth tables (user, session, account, verification from BetterAuth), trips, itinerary_days, activities, travel_segments, expenses, checklists, and more — every subsequent migration is an incremental diff on top.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle migrations are plain SQL files generated from schema diffs. They're ordered by filename prefix (`0000_`, `0001_`, ...) and tracked in `_journal.json`. Migrations are idempotent and run sequentially — never edit a committed migration; add a new one instead.

tour.title: Containerization & Local Dev Stack
tour.description: With the code understood, look at how it runs. The `Dockerfile` is a four-stage Bun build: an `install` stage pulls dependencies with a frozen lockfile, `build` compiles the Nuxt app, `migrate` runs `drizzle-kit migrate` against the live database (using the schema from Step 9), and `release` produces a slim production image that boots the Nitro server on port 3000 as a non-root user. For local development, `docker-compose.dev.yml` provisions Postgres 17 plus a Neon WebSocket proxy so the app can use the same Neon serverless driver locally that it uses in production.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds let each stage have its own base image and dependencies but only the final stage ends up in the published image. Putting `bun install` before `COPY . .` means Docker caches the dependency layer until `bun.lock` changes — rebuilds become seconds instead of minutes.

tour.title: Production Deployment & PWA
tour.description: The final stop covers the production edges. `vercel.json` registers the scheduled cron jobs (passport-expiry checks, visa-data refresh) that hit Nitro cron routes on a daily schedule. `pwa-assets.config.ts` configures the PWA asset generator that produces favicons and app icons from a single source image, completing the install-to-home-screen story the `app.vue` update prompt from Step 2 was hinting at. At this point you've followed a single user intent from the AI dock through the orchestration endpoint, the domain pipeline, the Google Maps facade, the Drizzle schema, the migrations, the container, and out to the deployment platform.
